Trees

Source: R/tree.R
tree.Rd

A tree is a hierarchy of nodes, such as an outline or a folder structure. Each node has an id, a position among its siblings, and a metadata map for its contents. Moving a node carries its whole subtree, and concurrent moves merge without creating cycles or duplicate nodes.

  • tree_create() creates a node, optionally with initial metadata, and returns its id.

  • tree_move() moves a node, with its subtree, to a new parent or position.

  • tree_delete() deletes a node and its descendants.

  • tree_meta() returns the node's metadata as a map handle (the metadata of a deleted node can still be read, but not changed), to be used with map_set(), map_get(), and the other map_* functions.

  • tree_children() returns the ids of a node's children in order, or of the root nodes when parent is NULL.

  • tree_nodes() returns a tibble of all nodes with columns id, parent (NA for root nodes), and index (the 1-based position among siblings).

  • tree_contains() reports whether a node exists and has not been deleted.

Node ids are strings of the form "counter@peer". They are stable and identical on every replica. A deleted node is gone for good, though: when undo() or doc_revert_to() brings back a deleted subtree, the nodes return with their structure and metadata but under new ids, so ids held from before the deletion no longer refer to anything. Undoing a move, and doc_checkout(), keep ids.

Usage

tree_create(tree, parent = NULL, index = NULL, meta = list())

tree_move(tree, node, parent = NULL, index = NULL)

tree_delete(tree, node)

tree_meta(tree, node)

tree_children(tree, parent = NULL)

tree_nodes(tree)

tree_contains(tree, node)

Arguments

tree

A tree handle, from doc_tree() or a parent container. A loro_doc is also accepted and stands for its default root container; see doc_text().

parent

The id of the parent node, or NULL for the top level.

index

A 1-based position among the parent's children, or NULL to place the node last. For a move it is the position the node ends up at.

meta

A named list of plain values to store in the new node's metadata map, as map_set() would.

node

A node id.

Value

tree_create() returns the new node id. tree_move() and tree_delete() return tree invisibly. tree_meta() returns a map handle, tree_children() a character vector, tree_nodes() a data frame, and tree_contains() a logical.

Examples

doc = loro_doc()
tree = doc_tree(doc, "outline")

intro = tree_create(tree, meta = list(title = "Introduction"))
methods = tree_create(tree, meta = list(title = "Methods"))
data = tree_create(tree, parent = intro, meta = list(title = "Data"))

tree_move(tree, data, parent = methods)
tree_meta(tree, data)$title
#> [1] "Data"
tree_nodes(tree)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>   id                    parent                index
#>   <chr>                 <chr>                 <int>
#> 1 0@4139655949870583164 NA                        1
#> 2 2@4139655949870583164 NA                        2
#> 3 4@4139655949870583164 2@4139655949870583164     1
tree_children(tree, methods)
#> [1] "4@4139655949870583164"
